subject: R5 follow-on closes BC/Alberta employer-sponsored privacy applicability gap
body: R5 follow-on research extends the initial completion packet with BC/Alberta private-sector applicability, employer-sponsored benefits, benefit-plan deemed consent, same-purpose service-provider processing, cross-border routing, and breach-regime differences. Key finding: employer sponsorship and benefit-plan membership do not create blanket authority for BenefitFlow member-private navigation, booking, claims, direct-billing disclosure, analytics, or employer visibility. BC PIPA s.8(2) and Alberta PIPA s.8(2.2) are narrow enrolment/coverage deemed-consent mechanisms; Alberta OIPC authority expressly limits the rule and does not extend it to a person requesting payment under a benefits plan. Recommended P0 refinement is a ProcessingAuthority object, sponsor-admin/member-private separation, transaction-level jurisdiction/data-route evaluation, constrained deemed-consent rules, employer access denial by default for individual service activity, and jurisdiction-aware incident handling. Findings remain research evidence and require manager/Primary disposition; production partner classifications require qualified legal review.
